questions.question: Which properties form the minimum tensor contract at a model boundary?
options: Only the number of elements
Shape, dtype, and semantic meaning
Only the Python variable name
The accelerator model and host name
questions.explanation: TensorFlow validates structural properties such as shape and dtype, while the application must also preserve what each dimension and feature means. Equal element counts do not make two inputs compatible.

questions.question: Why should a team test a training step both eagerly and through tf.function?
options: Eager execution always produces better model quality.
Graph execution disables automatic differentiation.
Python side effects, control flow, tracing, and state updates can behave differently across the two paths.
tf.function changes every float32 tensor to float64.
questions.explanation: Eager mode is easier to inspect, while tf.function traces TensorFlow operations into graphs. Parity tests catch Python-only behavior, unexpected retracing, and state-update differences before deployment.

questions.question: A tf.function creates many concrete graphs for variable-length batches. What is the most direct first control?
options: Add more Python print calls inside the function.
Delete the validation dataset.
Bound the accepted shapes with bucketing, padding, or an appropriate input_signature.
Increase the serving canary to 100%.
questions.explanation: A bounded shape contract reduces accidental polymorphism and retracing. The accepted variation must still match real data; an overly rigid signature can reject legitimate requests.

questions.question: After warmup, an input pipeline needs 18 ms per batch and the device step needs 27 ms. With effective prefetch overlap, what is the idealized steady-state step time?
options: 9 ms
18 ms
27 ms
45 ms
questions.explanation: When producer and consumer overlap, the slower stage sets the idealized steady-state time: max(18, 27) = 27 ms. Without overlap, the times would add to 45 ms.

questions.question: What belongs in a production-ready custom Keras layer contract?
options: Create new trainable variables on every call.
Ignore the training argument for dropout-like behavior.
Track variables on the layer, define training/inference behavior, and serialize constructor configuration.
Return a different output rank for every batch.
questions.explanation: Tracked state, explicit training behavior, stable tensor contracts, and serializable configuration let layers train, restore, clone, and export predictably.

questions.question: With synchronous data parallelism across four replicas, what must a throughput comparison state clearly?
options: Only the optimizer class
Whether batch size is global or per replica, plus the resulting effective batch
Only the number of Python files
The model's marketing category
questions.explanation: A global batch is split across replicas. Confusing global and per-replica values changes optimization behavior and makes throughput and convergence comparisons misleading.

questions.question: What makes a SavedModel useful as a serving boundary?
options: It automatically proves model quality.
It stores only a screenshot of the model graph.
It packages variables and callable graph signatures with named tensor inputs and outputs.
It guarantees every client sends valid features.
questions.explanation: SavedModel signatures define callable endpoints for inference runtimes such as TensorFlow Serving. Quality, client validation, rollout policy, and monitoring still require separate evidence.

questions.question: A canary TensorFlow Serving worker begins restarting from out-of-memory errors. Which response best contains the failure?
options: Continue promotion because offline accuracy passed.
Retry every request against the same failing worker.
Stop candidate routing and keep an independently loaded, known-good version serving.
Remove version labels from telemetry.
questions.explanation: An isolated candidate pool and warm reference version bound traffic impact and preserve recovery capacity. Offline quality cannot substitute for load, memory, and rollback gates.
